solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Staff of authority almost catching water animal

indicators.note: catching means the staff word closes round the shortened water word

parts.note: the mace is the ceremonial staff carried before officials and laid on the Commons table

indicators.note: almost means the Latin word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: aqua is the Latin word for water

explanation.surface: A rod of office nearly snags something in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The water is Latin: the mace is the ceremonial staff laid on the House of Commons table.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-tailed Old World monkey is a kind of animal, so the general term is a fair hypernym.

clue.text: Accepting Article, like a top ecclesiastic

indicators.note: accepting means the cone-shaped word takes the article inside it

parts.note: a spinning top has a cone shape, so like a top means cone-shaped
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A senior churchman graciously accepts an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is the spinning toy, not a senior figure, and the definition is only 'ecclesiastic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives describing things belonging to church law or clergy, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Hindu campaigner heading for shake-up after ousting English

indicators.note: for shake-up means the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
after ousting means the clue word heading first loses the English letter

explanation.surface: A Hindu activist sets out to shake things up once the English have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after ousting' takes E out of HEADING, leaving HADING, and 'for shake-up' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi, a Hindu, led the non-violent campaign for Indian independence.

clue.text: Where criminals ended up flogged, having cased diner

indicators.note: having cased means the sold word wraps round the diner word like a case

parts.note: flogged is British slang for sold
a caff is a British informal name for a cheap cafe

explanation.surface: Criminals who robbed a diner were beaten and ended up somewhere grim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' suggests whipping but means sold; a CAFF is a cheap British cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemned criminals were executed on a gallows platform, so it is where they met their end.

clue.text: Advantage given by 21 Easter Bunny films, edited with length cut

indicators.note: edited means the remaining letters of the three words are reworked into a new arrangement
with length cut means the L is removed from the film words

explanation.surface: Easter Bunny films, trimmed in the edit, prove popular with crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is CROWDS. 'with length cut' takes L out of FILMS, and 'edited' rearranges EASTERBUNNYFIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for the protection one gains by being one of many people.

clue.text: Top-class run with special pilot may take place here

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with letter I for the digit
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an ace is a fighter pilot with many kills

explanation.surface: A first-rate flight with a special pilot might happen up here.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-all-in-one: the wordplay's 'pilot' also sets the scene for the definition, the region where flying takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft fly within the region of sky above a country, so flying would take place there.

clue.text: Father raised vote for love goddess

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for a priest's title Father

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the vote word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: aye is a yes vote

explanation.surface: A father puts his hand up in favour of a goddess of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AYE upward to EYA.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess associated with love and fertility.

clue.text: Where the atmosphere is still rising, editor is someone devious

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the whole string reads upward, backwards

parts.note: an eel is a slippery, devious person

explanation.surface: An editor rises in a calm atmosphere, though he is a slippery customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns EDISEEL upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side of a hill or ship, away from the wind, has calm air.

clue.text: Approximately nothing in sparsely populated country

parts.note: ca is the abbreviation of circa, meaning approximately
nada is Spanish-derived slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Next to nobody lives in a thinly settled land.
explanation.definitionFit: This vast North American nation has a very low population density.

clue.text: Having something rammed down one's throat because fault briefly returned?

definitions.text: Having something rammed down one's throat

parts.note: for can mean because

indicators.note: returned means the shortened fault word is read backwards
briefly means the fault word loses its last letter

parts.note: a defect is a fault

explanation.surface: Someone forced to accept something wonders whether it was because a fault came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts DEFECT to DEFEC and 'returned' turns that into CEFED.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, being made to swallow food; figuratively, being made to accept ideas against one's will.

clue.text: Neck rings in weak light

indicators.note: in means the ring letters go inside the light word

parts.note: a candle gives only a weak light
two rings are two O shapes

explanation.surface: A neck adorned with rings glimmers in candlelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is a verb, to kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for kissing and cuddling amorously.

clue.text: Phlegmatic Conservative wearing tartan

indicators.note: wearing means the Conservative letter is inside the tartan word

parts.note: plaid is tartan cloth

explanation.surface: A calm Tory politician dressed in tartan.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a calm temperament that is not easily excited.

clue.text: Excessive desire of one after prize with heartless song

indicators.note: after means the one letter follows the prize word

parts.note: a cup is a sporting prize
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heartless means the song word loses its central letter

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a trophy with a soulless song shows too much longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle T of DITTY to give DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupidity is greed, an inordinate longing for wealth or possessions.

clue.text: Tilting incorporated with internal padding?

parts.note: Inc is the abbreviation for incorporated, used of companies
something with padding inside is lined

explanation.surface: A tilting company has padding inside, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something sloping or leaning at an angle.

clue.text: Devious concerning covers from then on

indicators.note: covers means the concerning phrase wraps round the from-then-on word

parts.note: in re is a Latin legal phrase meaning concerning
since means from that time onward

explanation.surface: A devious person covers up what happened from that point on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' is IN RE, the legal Latin, which 'covers' SINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devious is not sincere, being deceitful rather than honest.

clue.text: Was in charge with flanks set up in advance?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning beforehand
sided means having its sides or flanks formed

explanation.surface: A commander was in charge, having set up the flanks before battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a whimsical reading: split it as PRE-SIDED, sides arranged beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair or direct a meeting, so the past tense means was in charge.

clue.text: Not quite cool? Uncool person recalled issue

indicators.note: not quite means the cool word stops one letter short

parts.note: chill means cool

indicators.note: recalled means the uncool person word is read backwards

parts.note: a nerd is an unfashionable, uncool person

explanation.surface: A not-quite-cool person, an uncool one, recalled a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts CHILL to CHIL and 'recalled' turns NERD into DREN. 'issue' means offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense means offspring, one's sons and daughters.

clue.text: Leafy spot below hospital shelter

indicators.note: below in a down clue means the leafy spot word comes under the hospital letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an arbour is a shady bower of trees or climbing plants

explanation.surface: A leafy garden spot under the hospital offers shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A port where ships are safe from storms is a refuge, and to harbour is also to shelter.

clue.text: Get a report from US agent over importing cheese

indicators.note: importing means the turned agent word takes the cheese inside it
over in a down clue means the agent word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a Fed is a US federal agent, such as an FBI officer
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: An American agent is questioned about smuggling in cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means read upward, so the agent is reversed before the cheese goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone after a mission in order to obtain a full account of it.

clue.text: Dressed nice and loud, not ready for spring?

indicators.note: dressed means the words nice and loud are arranged, as a shop window is dressed

explanation.surface: Someone dressed nicely and loudly is not prepared for the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is a coiled metal spring, not the season: unwound, it cannot spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring stores energy only when wound tight, so one unwound is not ready to leap.

clue.text: Carriage pursuit overtakes one

indicators.note: overtakes means the pursuit word takes the one letter inside it

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A carriage chase in which one coach overtakes another.
explanation.definitionFit: A light horse-drawn vehicle, often open, is a type of carriage.

clue.text: Presses express triumph with Detective Sergeant

parts.note: to crow is to boast or gloat in triumph
DS is the abbreviation for the police rank Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: The newspapers gloat alongside a detective sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presses' is a plural noun, throngs of people, not newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a dense throng of people, so presses are throngs or masses.

clue.text: Somehow a less incomplete country

indicators.note: incomplete means only an inner stretch of the run Somehow a less is used, its ends left off

explanation.surface: A country that is somehow less than whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' signals the letters taken from within 'Somehow a less', dropping SOMEHO and the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The principality is one of the four constituent nations of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Tofu to bring on, skipping starter in bit of sweat?

indicators.note: in means the shortened word goes inside the sweat word

parts.note: a bead is a single drop of sweat

indicators.note: skipping starter means the bring on word loses its first letter

parts.note: to incur is to bring something on oneself

explanation.surface: Tofu, to bring on without a starter course, in a sweaty dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping starter' cuts INCUR to NCUR, which goes 'in' BEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is soya curd pressed into blocks, the same food under another name.

clue.text: Ex-leader collected icy cabinet, keeping French away

parts.note: a collected person is calm and cool

indicators.note: keeping away, split round French, means the French letters are kept out of the cabinet word
away completes keeping away, telling us the French letters are taken out of the cabinet word

parts.note: a fridge is a cold storage cabinet

explanation.surface: A former leader assembled a frosty cabinet that kept the French out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' means calm, not gathered; FRIDGE loses FR.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin Coolidge was the thirtieth President of the United States, a former leader.

clue.text: Origin of Sunni or Shia belief in long recitation

indicators.note: origin means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a creed is a formal statement of religious belief

explanation.surface: The roots of Sunni or Shia doctrine are told at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunni or Shia' both start with S, so either supplies the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, often tedious piece of writing or speech.

clue.text: Catholic suffering assured in these?

indicators.note: suffering suggests the word assured is knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A Catholic, confident of his faith, suffers on medieval holy wars.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-all-in-one: 'these' points back to the whole clue, the wars where an assured Catholic suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval holy wars were Christian military campaigns to the Holy Land.
